liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Jerry's wah-wah guitar work is described as a joy [15]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Bobby's performance avoids being too cheesy, which the reviewer always loves [10]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Tennessee Jed stands out in memory, while Good Lovin' and Casey Jones end the first set [14]
- **Next Time You See Me** (1 review): Song shares a honky-tonk feel with You Win Again and Cumberland Blues [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-03-21.sbd.miller.92395.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 210 min; rated 4.48/5 by 21 [1]. Said about its sound: Blues tunes carry a barroom band feel the band later lost; Initial mix has Bobby prominent while Jerry's guitar is invisible and voice is low; Recording buzzes throughout, mostly in the beginning, but remains bearable [5][13][14]
- **gd1972-03-21.136670.sbd.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 27 songs; 199 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1972-03-21.set2-sbd.Samaritano.32370.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 86 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Pigpen's vocal performance is described as classic, with the band knowing the changes [7]

## Around the show

- New York City crowds loved Pigpen and brought out the best in the band [7]
- Stream or printed setlist incorrectly swaps Chinatown Shuffle and Next Time You See Me [9]
- Bobby mentions new strings during tuning between Bertha and Black Throated Wind [13]
- Reviewer feels melancholy about the band and lead guitarist after reading Phil's book [15]
- Performance serves as the dress rehearsal for the upcoming Europe Tour [5]
- Band was evolving nightly during this period, showing early developmental stages of songs [8]
- This source has fewer problems than the Miller recording [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-03-21.sbd.miller.92395.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel [1]. Also: Bad hum from a grounding issue eventually gets fixed in the recording; Audio was cut during the intro to Chinatown Shuffle [1]
- **gd1972-03-21.136670.sbd.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: sbd > cassette master > dat(48k) [2]. Also: This version was provided by an anonymous source with relatively few problems [2]
- **gd1972-03-21.set2-sbd.Samaritano.32370.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: MSR>Dat>Dat>Sonic Solutions>CD [3]
